title: Rollout failure playbook: consolidated actions, telemetry debrief, and safety checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: After a canary rollout of model v2.7.1-backed routing (route-policy: predictive-latency), we observed a progressive degradation in inference correctness and tail latency for a subset of requests routed via shadow traffic. The rollout triggered partial auto-rollback but the rollback did not fully restore baseline behavior for ~2 hours. This ticket consolidates the incident debrief, the immediate mitigations we applied, and the set of runbook and automation changes required to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC - Canary rollout started for v2.7.1 at 5% traffic with predictive-latency routing
2026-03-01 09:25 UTC - Shadow traffic experiment toggled to 20% for parity checks
2026-03-01 09:38 UTC - Alert: transformer-infer service p95 latency > 500ms (baseline 120ms) and error-rate increase to 1.4%
2026-03-01 09:40 UTC - Observability: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 96% to 57% for canary nodes
2026-03-01 09:42 UTC - Automated rollback triggered (policy: latency>300ms for 3 consecutive minutes)
2026-03-01 09:43 UTC - Rollback started but one canary pool failed to drain due to ongoing long-lived batched requests
2026-03-01 10:10 UTC - Manual intervention: disable batching override on canary pool and force-drain stale connections
2026-03-01 11:05 UTC - Telemetry returned to baseline, rollback completed; follow-up monitoring window started (2h)
2026-03-01 13:30 UTC - Final verification: latency and error-rate within SLA, canary closed
observations: KV cache warming behavior changed when model v2.7.1 used quantized attention kernels combined with dynamic prefix caching: certain long common prefixes produced KV cache churn
Shadow traffic revealed a semantic drift metric (n-gram alignment score) spike for 7% of requests vs baseline, indicating subtle tokenizer-model mismatch for edge sequences
Auto-rollback acted based on latency SLO but did not include a correctness/semantic-drift signal leading to oscillation in some routes
Drain logic for batched connections is not idempotent; in-flight composite batches could keep canary instances pinned for >20 minutes
Routing policy allowed falling back to a variant (v2.7.1-quant-compat) that had not been vetted for long-sequence KV cache interaction
metrics: Canary observed p50: 95ms, p95: 560ms during failure window
Error-rate baseline: 0.03%, peak: 1.4% (inference failures + timeout retries)
KV cache hit-rate baseline: 96%, dropped to 57% on canary pool
Semantic-drift (n-gram alignment) baseline median: 0.92, canary spike median: 0.71 for affected subset
root_cause: Interaction between the v2.7.1 kernel selection path for quantized attention and the runtime's prefix-based KV cache warming led to excessive cache churn for certain input patterns. This increased memory pressure and introduced higher latency for tail requests. Auto-rollback was only latency-aware and lacked a secondary correctness or cache-stability condition; combined with non-idempotent drain behavior, that caused a prolonged recovery window.
immediate_mitigations: Triggered automated rollback (latency policy) and then executed manual disable of batching override on impacted canary pool
Force-drained and recycled the affected instances to clear KV cache state
Re-routed routing policy to serve fallback model v2.6.9 for affected customer segments until full validation
Adjusted shadow traffic percentage back to 5% to reduce noise for inflight experiments
runbook_updates: Add a pre-rollout validation step: synthetic sequence suite (long-tail prompts) that measures KV cache stability and semantic-drift against baseline
Extend auto-rollback policy to include a correctness signal: semantic-drift threshold + latency combined gating
Add a drain idempotency check and 'force-drain' procedure in the runbook with safe timeouts and circuit-breaker controls
Require kernel-compatibility matrix check for quantized kernels vs runtime cache heuristics before approving model variants for canary
Document a post-rollback verification checklist with explicit KV cache hit-rate and semantic-drift targets

longer_term_recommendations: Introduce a staged shadow-to-canary ramp with automated 'stability gates' (KV hit-rate, semantic-drift, resource usage) rather than single-metric gates
Maintain a compatibility registry for model variants that records tested kernel/runtime interactions
Invest in lightweight RTT-based canary verification that runs a parallel correctness pass for a sampled set of requests
Enhance chaos-testing for kernel/caching interactions in a dedicated infra sandbox prior to production rollouts
postmortem_notes: This incident highlights a recurring class of failures where micro-interactions between model kernels and runtime heuristics produce emergent behavior under real workloads. The mitigations are a blend of observability (semantic-drift), safer automation (multi-signal rollback), and operational hardening (idempotent drains, kernel-compat registry). We saw no customer data exposure and SLAs were restored within the agreed window. Follow-up tickets assigned above and slated into the March release train.
